Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I didn't ask how you were. You didn't answer my question. Who decided to enter the zero, and why didn't anyone call me first?
How do I wrap up this meeting?
You answer my question, and then I leave. Who entered the zero, Hale, and why wasn't I called first?
What happens after we finish? Do I get a summary?
You'll have my position in writing, and I'll want yours the same way. Right now I'm waiting on an answer, Hale. Who entered the zero?
